rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so the table is tuned more aggressively while respecting fftbench's profile: it is a small (6.3KB text, 11 functions) compute-dense benchmark whose hot loops (FFT, polynomial arithmetic) are runtime-sensitive, so SUB stays cheap and near-always applicable (low cost weights, high security/diversity), SPLIT and IGV act as low-overhead diversity multipliers that strengthen other passes, and FLA plus BCF are favored moderately with tempered runtime-cost weights so flattening and bogus control flow concentrate on the larger functions (polynomial operator*, inverse, fft) rather than saturating the tight inner loops. ICALL and IBR get strong security and diversity weights because static call/branch analysis is most valuable against reverse engineering here, but their runtime-cost weights are the highest in the table to keep indirect-dispatch overhead out of the FFT inner loops where the feature model identifies extreme execution frequency. CorrectnessRisk weights remain low across the board since round 0 showed no ICE or miscompile, allowing slightly bolder application than a first-round candidate would warrant; only IBR retains a modestly elevated risk weight because indirect branching interacts most with register allocation and relocations in this C++ binary.
